title: Bench screen runs long MLX work with no idle-timer or scene-phase handling. Auto-lock moves the app to background mid-run and Metal rejects the GPU work, so the app crashes
scenario: The user taps 'Run all models' (the default picker choice) and leaves the iPad alone. The run covers 5 catalog models, each with 2 loads, a warm-up and 3 workloads x 3 reps (4K prefill included), plus first-time downloads of about 7.7 GB. That takes many minutes. NodeService disables the idle timer only while 'Serve tasks' is on (applyIdleTimer: keepAwake && loop != nil), so in the usual case auto-lock fires after a few minutes. The scene goes .inactive and then .background while TokenIterator/prefill is still submitting Metal command buffers. iOS refuses background GPU submission (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorBackgroundExecutionNotPermitted). MLX's command-buffer completion check throws a C++ error, which terminates the process. The whole run is lost and no receipt is saved for the model in progress. The fleet path pauses on background; the UI path has no equivalent.
evidence: BenchCoordinator.run (lines 93-128) only acquires GPUGate and loops over the entries. Nothing in Bench/* or BenchView sets UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled or watches scenePhase. The only idle-timer code is NodeService.applyIdleTimer (NodeService.swift:118), and the only scene handling is AppModel.shared.node.scenePhaseChanged (AgentConsoleApp.swift:52). Batches use BGContinuedProcessingTask for background GPU; Bench uses nothing.
fix: While isRunning, set UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true and restore it in finish(). Forward scenePhase to the coordinator: on .inactive, set the cancel flag and also cancel `task`, so the token loop's Task.isCancelled check breaks between tokens. Optionally wrap the run in beginBackgroundTask only long enough to save the partial receipt.
notes:
UPHELD(medium): I could not refute the claim. On origin/bench, BenchCoordinator.run (BenchCoordinator.swift ~93-128) only acquires GPUGate and then loops runner.run over the entries. Its only stop signal is a CancelFlag that the user sets from the Cancel button. A `git grep` across the bench branch's ios tree for idleTimer, scenePhase, beginBackgroundTask and BGContinued returns only these:
- NodeService.applyIdleTimer (line 118): `isIdleTimerDisabled = keepAwake && loop != nil`, so it is on only while the fleet loop is serving.
- NodeService.scenePhaseChanged (lines 77-100): on .background it stops only the node loop (`guard loop != nil else { return }`).
- AgentConsoleApp.swift:46-52: forwards scenePhase only to node.
- ContinuedProcessing.swift: batches only.
- JobsViews: UI refresh only.

Nothing in Bench/* or BenchView disables auto-lock or reacts to scene changes. The project.yml entitlement com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu covers GPU work only inside a BGContinuedProcessingTask, and the bench run is not wrapped in one.

A multi-model run (downloads, 4K prefill, 3x3 reps) easily lasts longer than the auto-lock interval. When the device locks, the app goes to background while MLX is still submitting Metal command buffers. iOS rejects background GPU submission with "Insufficient Permission". MLX's command-buffer completion check throws, which aborts the process. This is a known crash pattern for MLX apps on iOS. The run is lost, and so is the receipt for the model in progress, because receipts are saved only after runner.run returns.

The code path is fully confirmed. The terminate-on-background-GPU behavior comes from known MLX/iOS behavior, not an on-device repro, so confidence is medium rather than high. | fix: In BenchCoordinator.run, set UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true. In finish(), restore it to NodeService's keepAwake && loop state, or recompute that state, rather than setting it to false unconditionally, so the node's setting is not clobbered. Add a BenchCoordinator.scenePhaseChanged(_:) and call it from AgentConsoleApp's onChange. On .inactive or .background it should call cancelFlag.set() and task?.cancel(), and hold a beginBackgroundTask only long enough for the current token step to return and the partial receipt to be saved. Make sure BenchmarkRunner's token loop checks isCancelled between tokens, not only between reps.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this claim. On origin/bench, BenchCoordinator.run (BenchCoordinator.swift:93-128) acquires GPUGate and loops BenchmarkRunner over the entries. A grep of origin/bench ios/ for idleTimer, scenePhase, beginBackgroundTask and BGContinued finds only these: NodeService.applyIdleTimer (line 118, `keepAwake && loop != nil`, so it applies only while Serve tasks is on), NodeService.scenePhaseChanged, the BatchCoordinator pause in AgentConsoleApp.swift:46-52, ContinuedProcessing (batches only), and JobsViews. BenchView.swift has nothing about screen, lock, awake or background. Nothing on the bench branch disables the idle timer or reacts to scene phase.

The app already knows Metal work dies in background. AgentConsoleApp.swift:47-48 says "Foreground-only batches stop at a file boundary instead of being killed mid-generation (Metal work isn't allowed in background)". NodeService pauses on background for the same reason. MLX on iOS turns a background command-buffer submission error into a thrown C++ error inside the Metal completion handler, which terminates the process. A BenchmarkRunner catch block cannot recover from that.

A full-catalog run (several models, two loads each, a warm-up, 3 workloads x 3 reps including 4K prefill, and first-time downloads) easily outlasts the iPad's auto-lock interval. So a run left unattended will background mid-prefill or mid-decode and crash. The model in progress gets no receipt; earlier models' receipts are already saved. Mitigating factor: the user may have auto-lock set to Never, or may keep touching the screen. That is not the default, so the defect stands. Severity high is reasonable, medium at minimum. | fix: In BenchCoordinator.run, set UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true. In finish(), restore it without clobbering NodeService: re-run node.applyIdleTimer, or compute `bench.isRunning || (keepAwake && loop != nil)`. In AgentConsoleApp's onChange(of: scenePhase), forward .background (or .inactive) to bench, which then calls cancelFlag.set() and task?.cancel(). The runner then stops between reps or tokens and writes a "cancelled" receipt. Optionally wrap that in beginBackgroundTask so the save can finish.

UPHELD(medium): I could not refute this, so I'm confirming it. I checked origin/bench after `git fetch`.

1. Nothing keeps the device awake during a bench run. BenchCoordinator.run (BenchCoordinator.swift:93-128) acquires GPUGate, loops over the entries with BenchmarkRunner, then releases the gate. It never touches UIApplication.isIdleTimerDisabled. Searching for idleTimer, scenePhase and background on the branch finds only one idle-timer writer: NodeService.applyIdleTimer at NodeService.swift:117-118, which sets the flag to `keepAwake && loop != nil`. So it is true only while "Serve tasks" is on. With the node off, which is the usual bench case, the default auto-lock (2-5 min on iPad) still runs. A progress bar does not reset the idle timer; only touches do.

2. Nothing reacts when the app leaves the foreground. AgentConsoleApp.swift:46-52 forwards scenePhase only to BatchCoordinator.pauseForeground (and only when there is no background GPU) and to node.scenePhaseChanged. BenchCoordinator gets no notification, and there are no beginBackgroundTask or BGContinuedProcessing calls under Bench/.

3. The codebase already treats this failure as real. The comment at AgentConsoleApp.swift:47-48 says "Metal work isn't allowed in background", and NodeService pauses its loop on .background. ContinuedProcessing.swift:50-52 says background MLX "would fail" without background GPU. MLX's Metal backend checks command-buffer status in the completion handler and throws ("Insufficient Permission (to submit GPU work from background)"). That throw happens on a Metal callback thread, so it terminates the process. The bench is the one long GPU path with none of these protections.

4. A run is long enough for auto-lock to fire. Running all catalog models means, per model, possible multi-GB downloads, loads, a warm-up, and workloads x reps including 4K prefill. That is many minutes with no touch input. Receipts are saved only after `runner.run` returns (`await store(receipt)`), so the model in progress loses its receipt. Earlier models keep theirs.

Caveats, which is why confidence is medium:
- I can't reproduce on a device here.
- If the user set Auto-Lock to Never, or "Serve tasks" is on with keepAwake, the scenario doesn't happen.
- The outcome could be an MLX error or a hang instead of a hard crash, depending on where suspension lands. Even then the run and that model's receipt are lost.

Severity: medium-high. This is a new feature with likely data loss or a crash in ordinary unattended use.

One limit of the proposed fix: cancelFlag is checked only between reps (per the "Stopping after the current rep" text). Cancelling on .inactive alone could still leave a 4K prefill in flight when the app is suspended. Disabling the idle timer while the run is going is the main fix. | fix: In BenchCoordinator.run, set UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true when isRunning becomes true. In finish(), restore it, leaving it on if the node needs it (call NodeService.applyIdleTimer or re-evaluate `node.keepAwake && node serving`), so the bench doesn't undo the node's setting. Forward scenePhase from AgentConsoleApp to the coordinator. On .background, set cancelFlag, cancel `task`, and wrap the shutdown in beginBackgroundTask/endBackgroundTask so the current rep can stop and a partial receipt can be saved.

title: During a benchmark the chat model can be reloaded outside the GPU gate, so it is resident and evaluating alongside the measured model
scenario: A bench (UI or fleet) holds GPUGate and has called backend.unload(), so container is nil and isLoaded is false. The user switches to the Chat tab, which re-runs `.task(id: selectedModelID)`. That calls `backend.load` WITHOUT the gate. The chat model (about 1 GB, or 4.85 GB for LFM2.5-8B) is then loaded and eval'd on another thread while BenchmarkRunner is in a timed rep or is itself loading. Effects: (a) receipts record wrong peak footprint, available memory and tok/s, because the GPU is shared with weight eval, and the design assumes 'only the measured model may be resident'; (b) two big models can push past the jetsam limit; (c) MLX eval runs from two threads at once, which is exactly what GPUGate exists to prevent. A related leak: LocalAgent.run keeps a local `conversation` across tool steps and confirmations. If the bench grabs the gate while a chat waits for tool approval, invalidateConversation() does not free that session, so the old chat weights stay resident for the entire bench.
evidence: On integration, ChatView.swift:52-56 does `guard !(await backend.isLoaded) else { return }; try? await backend.load {...}` with no GPUGate.acquire. MLXBackend.unload() (bench MLXBackend.swift:94) makes isLoaded false. BenchmarkRunner never re-checks the footprint against the baseline after unload. PR #6 (fix-node) adds the gate to this exact call, which confirms it is a known race. PR #7 makes it routine, because every bench run unloads the chat model.
fix: Gate the ChatView load (take the fix-node change) before or together with #7. In addition, have MLXBackend.unload() set a 'suspended' flag that makes load() wait or refuse until the bench calls a resume(). Record in the receipt any footprint delta above the baseline after unload.
notes:
UPHELD(high): I confirmed the claim from the code at the cited refs.

1. **Ungated load in ChatView.** On origin/integration, ChatView.swift:55-59 is a `.task(id: selectedModelID)` block. It checks `backend.isLoaded` and then calls `backend.load` without taking GPUGate.

2. **The task re-runs when the user switches tabs during a bench.** On PR #7 (branch `bench`), RootView is a TabView with "Agent" as the first tab and "Bench" as its own tab. SwiftUI cancels a tab's `.task` when the tab disappears and starts it again when the tab reappears. So the sequence is: the user opens Bench and taps Run, then switches back to Agent, and the task runs again.

3. **The chat model reads as unloaded during the bench.** BenchCoordinator.run takes the gate and then calls `BenchmarkRunner.run`. At BenchmarkRunner.swift:73 that calls `backend.unload()`, which sets `container = nil` and bumps `epoch`. `isLoaded` is therefore false, so ChatView calls `load()`.

4. **The chat weights get installed while the bench runs.** `load()` reads `startEpoch` after the unload, so the epoch check passes and the chat container is installed. Meanwhile `BenchmarkRunner` is running `loadContainer` or a timed `decode` on its own task, with nothing serializing the two. Two MLX weight loads/evals can then run at once and two models are resident together. This invalidates `footprintAfterLoadBytes`, `peakFootprintBytes`, `available` and tok/s, and with LFM2.5-8B it raises jetsam risk. The baseline and headroom check happens only once, right after unload, so a chat load that starts later is never detected.

5. **The secondary leak is also real.** In `LocalAgent.run` (LocalAgent.swift on bench), the gate is held only for setup and while tokens stream. It is released between tool steps and during `pendingConfirmation`, while the local `let conversation` keeps a strong reference to the ChatSession and its container. The bench can take the gate during a tool-approval wait. `invalidateConversation()` only clears `self.conversation`, so the old weights stay resident through the bench.

Medium severity is appropriate: the bug corrupts receipts and the app could be killed (jetsam) for using too much memory, but it needs the user to switch tabs during a run. | fix: Wrap the ChatView `.task` load in `await GPUGate.shared.acquire("chat load")` / `release()` (the PR #6 change) and re-check `isLoaded` after acquiring the gate. Merge this before or together with #7. Optionally, have MLXBackend keep a `suspended` flag that `unload()` sets and the bench clears when it finishes; `load()` would throw or no-op while it is set. Also re-sample `physFootprint` before each rep and record it in the receipt if it rises above the baseline by more than a threshold.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. Every link in the claimed chain holds when I read the code.
1) On origin/integration, ChatView.swift:52-56 runs `.task(id: selectedModelID)` with `guard !(await backend.isLoaded) else { return }` and then `try? await backend.load{...}`. Nothing acquires GPUGate on that path.
2) On origin/bench, BenchCoordinator.run acquires GPUGate and then calls BenchmarkRunner.run. That calls `backend.unload()` (MLXBackend.swift on the bench branch), which sets container to nil and increments epoch. So isLoaded becomes false.
3) Bench is a separate tab in RootView's TabView, so to start a run the user has to be on the Bench tab. SwiftUI cancels `.task` when its view disappears and starts it again when the view reappears. Returning to the Agent tab during a run therefore re-runs the load closure, isLoaded is false, and MLXBackend.load() runs.
4) Nothing stops that load. load() calls reconcileSelection(), which does nothing because the selection is unchanged. It then captures the current epoch, which already includes the bench's increment, so the `epoch == startEpoch` check passes and the chat container gets installed. That load evaluates its weights on another task while BenchmarkRunner is loading or decoding.
5) The receipts are corrupted as a result. BenchmarkRunner sets MLX.Memory.peakMemory = 0 and calls clearCache() globally, and samples physFootprint and availableMemory for the whole process. The chat model's weights therefore land in peakFootprint, mlxPeak, footprintAfterLoad and minAvailable, and its eval competes with the timed reps. A large chat model plus a large bench model also raises the jetsam risk.
6) PR #6 (fix-node) adds GPUGate acquire and release around exactly this load. With that change the load waits until the bench releases the gate. This confirms both the bug and the fix.
7) The secondary leak is admitted in the code itself. The comment in unload() reads "conversations still holding it keep it alive until they end". invalidateConversation() cannot release a `conversation` that LocalAgent.run holds locally.
Severity medium is right. The trigger is common (switching tabs during a multi-minute bench), the main effect is wrong receipts, and the jetsam or MLX-concurrency crash only happens sometimes.
Merge hazard to note: fix-node uses `try await GPUGate.shared.acquire(...)` (throwing), while bench uses `await GPUGate.shared.acquire("benchmark")` (non-throwing). The GPUGate signature therefore has to be reconciled when #6 and #7 are merged together. | fix: Apply fix-node's ChatView change with or before #7: acquire GPUGate.shared before backend.load in the `.task(id:)` and release it afterwards, and reconcile the acquire signature (throwing in #6, non-throwing in #7). Optionally, have BenchmarkRunner check physFootprint against the baseline before each rep and record or abort if it has grown more than a set amount after unload. That would also catch a chat session that is still held during a pending tool confirmation, for example by having BenchCoordinator cancel or wait for agent.run, not just call invalidateConversation().

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. The failing path holds up step by step.

1. RootView (AgentConsoleApp.swift on origin/bench) is a TabView. "Agent" (ChatView) and "Bench" (BenchView) are separate tabs. When a tab reappears, SwiftUI restarts the view's `.task(id: selectedModelID)` on appear.

2. A UI bench starts like this. BenchCoordinator.run acquires GPUGate("benchmark") and calls onModelUnloaded. BenchmarkRunner.run (BenchmarkRunner.swift:73) then calls `backend.unload()`. That sets `container = nil` and `epoch += 1`, so `isLoaded` becomes false. `unload()` only exists on the bench branch; integration has no unload, so PR #7 introduces this state.

3. The user switches to the Agent tab. ChatView.swift:52-56 (identical on integration and bench, since #7 does not touch ChatView) does `guard !(await backend.isLoaded) else { return }; try? await backend.load {...}`. It never acquires GPUGate.

4. `MLXBackend.load` calls `reconcileSelection()`, which is a no-op because the selection is unchanged. It reads `startEpoch` after the bench's unload already bumped epoch, runs `loadContainer`, which downloads, loads and evals the weights, and then installs the container because epoch still equals startEpoch. Nothing in MLXBackend blocks load while a bench holds the gate.

5. This load runs while BenchmarkRunner is in its own `loadContainer`, warm-up or timed decode reps. Two models are then resident, and MLX work runs from two threads at once, which GPUGate exists to prevent. Because the free-memory check ran before the chat model loaded, the bench's 1.5 GB headroom check no longer protects against jetsam. The receipt's peakFootprint, availableAfterLoad and tok/s include the chat model's load. Nothing re-checks the footprint against the baseline, so the receipt does not flag this.

The secondary claim, that a held LocalAgent conversation keeps the old weights alive, is plausible but I did not need it. The main path above is enough.

Medium severity is fair: it skews receipts and can cause jetsam or a concurrent-MLX crash, and it is triggered just by switching tabs during a bench. | fix: Have ChatView's `.task` acquire the gate around the load: `await GPUGate.shared.acquire("chat load"); defer-release; if !(await backend.isLoaded) { try? await backend.load ... }`. This is the change PR #6 already makes, so land it together with or before #7. To keep other callers out as well, add a `suspended` flag to MLXBackend: `unload()` sets it, `load()` waits or throws while it is set, and BenchCoordinator.finish clears it. Optionally record a warning in the receipt when physFootprint after the rep is more than the baseline plus the measured model.

title: Bench unload silently drops an applied federated LoRA adapter, and the trainer's ObjectIdentifier check can match a new container
scenario: The user taps 'Use federated adapter'. NodeService.useFederatedAdapter converts the chat container to LoRA and loads the round's weights, and Settings shows 'Using round rXXXX'. The user then runs any benchmark, or the fleet sends a bench task. BenchmarkRunner calls backend.unload(), the chat container (with the adapter) is freed, and the next chat message reloads base weights. Chat now answers from the base model while adapterStatus still says the round is in use. Separately, FederatedTrainer.applied keys on ObjectIdentifier(container) of the freed container. Bench allocates and frees two more containers before the chat reloads, so a reused address can make ensureAdapter() return early on a fresh, unconverted model. The next train_lora/loadAdapter then fails with unused-key errors, or trains a model that has no LoRA layers.
evidence: MLXBackend.unload(): `container = nil; epoch += 1`, with no notification to FederatedTrainer. FederatedTrainer.ensureAdapter: `if let a = applied, a.container == ObjectIdentifier(c) { ... return }`. The bench path calls unload unconditionally (BenchmarkRunner.swift:73). PR #6 adds a chat-adapter snapshot/restore that this unload also bypasses.
fix: In unload(), clear trainer.applied (or keep a strong reference or generation counter instead of ObjectIdentifier) and reset NodeService.adapterStatus. Better: after the bench, reapply the adapter that was active (snapshot its bytes before unloading), or refuse to unload while a federated adapter is in use.
notes:
UPHELD(medium): I checked this against origin/bench and the main part of the claim holds. MLXBackend.unload() (MLXBackend.swift:94) sets `container = nil` and increments `epoch`. Nothing is sent to FederatedTrainer and nothing resets NodeService.adapterStatus. BenchmarkRunner.run calls backend.unload() unconditionally (BenchmarkRunner.swift:73). NodeService.runBench calls onModelChanged() before and after the run, which goes through agent.invalidateConversation() (AgentConsoleApp.swift:22). That means no chat conversation keeps the old LoRA-converted container alive, so it is freed. The next chat load goes through MLXBackend.loadContainer and loads base weights only. useFederatedAdapter is the only path that applies the round adapter, so it is gone, while adapterStatus still says "Using round …" (NodeService.swift:515). The user sees no error. Chat just quietly answers from the base model. The same loss already happened before this PR when the user switched models with selectModel. What PR #7 adds is two new triggers that run without the user touching the chat model: the Bench screen and fleet bench tasks.

The ObjectIdentifier part holds up structurally. FederatedTrainer.Applied stores ObjectIdentifier(container) (FederatedTrainer.swift:48,73-74) and keeps no strong reference. After unload, `applied` stays stale. In ensureAdapter, `a.container == ObjectIdentifier(c)` compares a freed object's address with the new container's address. If the allocator reuses that address, which is likely after the bench allocates and frees two containers of the same class, ensureAdapter returns early on an unconverted model. loadAdapter then fails because `.noUnusedKeys` rejects the lora_a and lora_b keys, or train has no LoRA parameters. Address reuse depends on timing, so I can't prove it fires every time, but the code path exists. When the addresses differ, the result is milder but still wrong: the model is re-converted and resetToInitial works, but the in-use status shown to the user is false.

Severity: medium, because it is silent wrong behaviour after a common action (running a benchmark). | fix: 1. In FederatedTrainer, replace `ObjectIdentifier` with a strong `weak var`, or a weak-reference check (`weak var container: ModelContainer?` plus `===`). The simplest alternative is a generation counter that MLXBackend increments in both unload() and the selectModel path. ensureAdapter then compares generations.
2. Add `FederatedTrainer.invalidate()`, which sets `applied = nil`. Call it from NodeService.runBench and from the BenchCoordinator path after the run.
3. In the same place, set `adapterStatus = nil` or "Adapter unloaded by benchmark; tap Use federated adapter again". A better option is to re-run useFederatedAdapter's apply step from cached round bytes after the bench finishes.

UPHELD(high): I confirmed this on origin/bench. Nothing in the PR guards against it.

1. **The adapter is dropped silently.** `MLXBackend.unload()` at MLXBackend.swift:94 does `container = nil; epoch += 1; clearCache()`. Nothing tells `FederatedTrainer` or `NodeService`. `BenchmarkRunner.swift:73` always calls `backend.unload()`. Both the Bench screen and fleet `runBench` reach it, and `runBench` also calls `onModelChanged()`, which is `agent.invalidateConversation()`. That drops the last conversation, which was the last strong reference to the old container (the one carrying the LoRA layers), so it is freed. Nothing in BenchmarkRunner, BenchView or `runBench` reapplies the adapter afterwards. The next `ensureLoaded` and `load()` call `loadContainer` and get base weights. `NodeService.adapterStatus` still reads "Using round rXXXX". So chat answers from the base model while the UI says the federated adapter is in use. This bug is concrete and deterministic.

2. **The stale-identity half holds but is probabilistic.** `FederatedTrainer.Applied` stores only `ObjectIdentifier(c)` and keeps no strong reference to the container. Once the container is freed, its address can be reused. BenchmarkRunner loads two containers and frees both, then chat reloads a third, so the same allocation size is reused several times. If the new container gets the old address, `ensureAdapter` (`if let a = applied, a.container == id { return }`) returns early on a model that was never converted to LoRA. Then `loadAdapter`/`resetToInitial` fail with an unused-keys error from `verify: [.noUnusedKeys]`, or `train` runs on a model that has no LoRA layers. Even without address reuse, `applied` keeps a stale `adapterSummary`.

3. **Partly pre-existing, but this PR makes it routine.** `reconcileSelection` already had the same problem when switching models. PR #7 adds a new path that unloads the same model during normal use: a bench run, or any bench task the fleet sends.

**Severity:** medium is right. | fix: Three changes:

1. **Track container identity safely.** Give `MLXBackend` a `containerGeneration`, bumped in `load`, `unload` and `reconcileSelection`. `FederatedTrainer.Applied` stores that generation, or holds a weak or strong reference to the container, instead of `ObjectIdentifier`.
2. **Clear stale state in `runBench`.** Before calling `BenchmarkRunner`, record whether a federated adapter is active. Clear `trainer.applied` and set `adapterStatus` to something like "Adapter unloaded by benchmark — tap again to reapply".
3. **Optionally restore the adapter.** After the bench, reload the model and reapply the last applied round's bytes under `GPUGate`.

UPHELD(high): I confirmed this against origin/bench (PR #7). The adapter-loss half is certain. The address-reuse half is real but depends on the allocator.

How the adapter is lost:
1. NodeService.useFederatedAdapter (NodeService.swift ~486-515) calls trainer.ensureAdapter. That converts the backend's current container to LoRA in place and records `Applied(container: ObjectIdentifier(c), ...)`. loadAdapter then installs the round's weights, and adapterStatus is set to "Using round X".
2. The user starts a bench from BenchCoordinator, or the fleet sends a bench task (NodeService.runBench ~331-351). BenchmarkRunner.run calls backend.unload() unconditionally at BenchmarkRunner.swift:73.
3. MLXBackend.unload (MLXBackend.swift:94-100) is new in this PR. It only does `container = nil; epoch += 1; clearCache`. It does not notify FederatedTrainer and does not touch NodeService.adapterStatus. onModelChanged only invalidates the chat conversation.
4. The next chat message calls ensureLoaded/load. isLoaded is false, so loadContainer brings back plain base weights. Chat now answers from the base model while Settings still shows "Using round X". Nothing in the code reapplies the adapter.

Why ensureAdapter can match the wrong container:
- FederatedTrainer stores only ObjectIdentifier(c) and never holds a strong reference, so the old container can be freed.
- Bench creates and frees two containers of the same class (first load, then warm reload), and the chat reload then creates a third. The allocator can hand that new ModelContainer the freed address.
- If it does, `applied.container == ObjectIdentifier(c)` matches and ensureAdapter returns early on a base model with no LoRA layers. The next loadAdapter fails `.noUnusedKeys` because the lora_a/lora_b keys don't exist on that model. train_lora would train a model with no LoRA layers, or fail. In both cases the user cannot recover without relaunching the app.
- Whether this happens is up to the allocator, but nothing in the code prevents it. A model switch (reconcileSelection) has the same weakness on integration already. PR #7 adds a new, common, unconditional path to it, triggered by the user or the fleet.
- If the address is not reused, a fresh conversion happens with the seed and the trainer recovers. Even then, the visible staleness from the first half remains.

Severity: medium is right. Nothing crashes, but the chat model's identity changes silently and the UI reports the wrong state. | fix: 1. Replace `Applied.container: ObjectIdentifier` with either a strong `ModelContainer` reference compared with `===`, or a load-generation counter taken from MLXBackend (bump it in unload, reconcileSelection and load). Then a freed address can never match a new container.
2. Give MLXBackend.unload a hook, for example an `onUnload` closure or a generation that NodeService observes. NodeService then clears adapterStatus, or better marks it "Adapter dropped by benchmark".
3. Optionally, have BenchmarkRunner and NodeService remember the active round id and its bytes before unloading, and run ensureAdapter + loadAdapter again after the bench. The other option is to refuse to bench while a federated adapter is applied.

title: Merge hazard with #2 (inkling2) and #6 (fix-node): bench's static loadContainer/unload bypass their single-flight, draining, VLM and memory-budget load paths
ref: PR #7 vs PR #2 / PR #6 (textual conflict in MLXBackend.load)
scenario: Both #2 and #6 rewrite MLXBackend.load, and git merge-tree reports a conflict in MLXBackend.swift against bench for both. If the conflict is resolved by keeping bench's `static loadContainer(for:)` (`#huggingFaceLoadModelContainer`, LLM factory only): (1) the catalog Inkling entries (loader: .vlm, `inkling2_loop`) are benchmarked through the LLM factory and fail to load, or skip MemoryBudget.fit and the memoryLimit cap that #2 relies on to avoid jetsam on a 10 GB model. BenchCoordinator explicitly says Inkling will be 'included automatically'. (2) unload() only bumps epoch. It does not cancel the `inflight`/`loading` task or append it to `draining`, so a chat load already in flight keeps allocating while bench loads its own copy, which is the memory doubling #2's draining exists to prevent. (3) BenchmarkRunner's TokenIterator ignores entry.prefillStepSize and prefill chunking (#2 applyMemorySettings), so Inkling receipts measure a configuration the app never uses.

title: Receipt upload has no retry, and the worker does not dedupe, so manual re-upload after an ambiguous failure creates duplicate receipts
scenario: The worker is briefly unreachable, or the 30 s request times out after the server already wrote the file. The bench records 'Upload failed', with no automatic retry and no pending-upload queue, so the receipt reaches the worker only if the user later taps 'Upload to worker' on each receipt. A re-upload after a timeout where the server did save creates a second file with a new name and the same receipt_id. list_receipts then reports the run twice, which biases any aggregation Claude does over receipts.
evidence: ReceiptStore.upload is called once per receipt with no retry, in both BenchCoordinator.store and NodeService.runBench. receipts.py save() always writes a new `<stamp>-<model>[-n].json` and never checks receipt_id.
fix: Make the worker idempotent on receipt_id: return the existing name if it was already stored. On the iPad, keep an 'uploaded' marker per receipt and retry pending ones on the next run or app activation.
notes:
UPHELD(high): I confirmed this at origin/bench (PR #7), and it holds at low severity.

1. BenchCoordinator.swift:49-63: `ReceiptStore.upload` sends a single POST with `timeoutInterval = 30` and has no retry. `BenchCoordinator.upload` (line 146-151) catches the error and only sets `uploadStatus[name] = "Upload failed: ..."`.
2. NodeService.swift:356-358 also calls it once and only logs on failure. No pending or "uploaded" marker is kept anywhere. The only way to retry is the manual "Upload to worker" button in BenchView.swift:166.
3. worker/receipts.py `save()` (around line 64) always builds a new `<stamp>-<model>[-n].json` name, adding a suffix when the name collides. It never reads `receipt_id`, so posting the same body twice stores two files.
4. BenchReceipt.swift:28 shows each receipt has a stable `receiptId`, so deduping on it is possible.
5. `summarize()` leaves out `receipt_id`, so `list_receipts` (mcp_bridge.py:532-542) shows the duplicates as two separate runs, and whoever reads the list cannot tell they are the same run.

The duplicate case does not even need a timeout. A user who taps upload again after a success also gets a second copy. Data loss is limited because the receipt stays on the iPad, and the impact is skewed aggregates and clutter, so low severity is right. | fix: In receipts.py `save()`, take `receipt_id` from the JSON. While holding the lock, check an index (receipt_id to name, built from the existing files at startup or kept in a sidecar file). If the id is already stored, return the existing name, either as 200 with `{"name": existing, "bytes": n, "duplicate": true}` or as 201. Also add `receipt_id` to `summarize()`. On iOS (optional), store the name returned by the worker next to each saved receipt, and re-upload receipts that have no stored name on the next bench run or when the app becomes active.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute the claim, and the code on origin/bench supports it.

- **Every save makes a new file.** `ReceiptStore.save` in `worker/receipts.py` (around lines 64-85) parses the receipt and builds a name from a timestamp and the model id. Inside the lock, it adds a `-n` suffix only to avoid overwriting an existing file of the same name. It never reads or checks `receiptId`/`receipt_id`, so sending the same receipt twice produces two files.
- **Each receipt has a stable id the worker could use.** `BenchReceipt.swift:11` declares `receiptId`, and `BenchmarkRunner.swift:275` sets it once per receipt to a random UUID.
- **Upload is a single attempt.** `BenchCoordinator.swift:53` sets `timeoutInterval = 30`. `BenchCoordinator.upload` and the `NodeService.runBench` path each call `ReceiptStore.upload` once. On failure they only record "Upload failed" or log the error. Nothing marks a receipt as uploaded and nothing retries it later. The only recovery is the manual "Upload to worker" button.
- **Nothing downstream filters duplicates.** `list()` returns every file whose name matches `NAME`. `summarize()` leaves out `receipt_id`, so a reader such as Claude's `list_receipts` tool cannot easily tell a duplicate from a real second run. It would have to notice the identical `created_at` and model.

How it fails: the server writes the file, but the response is lost or arrives after the 30 s timeout. The iPad shows "Upload failed", the user taps "Upload to worker" again, and two receipts now describe one run. That double-counts the run in any aggregate.

Severity is low because it needs a manual re-upload after a timeout or lost response, and no data is lost. The suggested fix is correct. | fix: In `worker/receipts.py` `save()`: if `receipt.get("receipt_id")` is a string, then inside the lock look for an existing receipt with that id and return `{"name": existing, "bytes": ..., "duplicate": True}` instead of writing a second file. To find it, keep an in-memory id-to-name index built at startup by scanning the stored receipts, or write the file as `<stamp>-<model>-<receipt_id[:8]>.json` and glob for `*-<receipt_id[:8]>.json`. Also add `receipt_id` to `summarize()`. On the iPad, optionally store an "uploaded" marker next to each receipt file and retry the ones without it when the app becomes active or after the next bench run. Once the worker is idempotent, those retries are safe.

UPHELD(high): I confirmed the defect on origin/bench. On the iPad, ReceiptStore.upload in BenchCoordinator.swift makes one URLSession POST with a 30 s timeout. It has no retry. Neither BenchCoordinator.store nor NodeService.runBench re-tries a failed upload or records that an upload is pending. The only other path to the worker is the manual "Upload to worker" button in BenchView. That button calls coordinator.upload(saved.url) again with nothing stopping a second upload: it stays tappable after "Uploaded as …" and the result is kept only in memory.

On the worker, receipts.py ReceiptStore.save (around lines 64-84) checks the size, the JSON and schema==1. It then always writes a new `<stamp>-<model>[-n].json`, and the stamp is the server's current time. It never reads `receiptId`, which BenchReceipt.swift does carry (`var receiptId: String`).

Failing scenario:
1. A bench run saves the receipt and POSTs it.
2. The server writes the file, but the response is lost or the 30 s timeout fires. The app shows "Upload failed".
3. The user taps "Upload to worker". The server writes a second file with a new stamp and the same receiptId.

The same thing happens without any failure if the user simply taps the button twice. GET /receipts and the MCP `list_receipts` tool then return both entries. summarize() leaves out receipt_id, so a consumer of the listing cannot even tell they are duplicates, and any aggregation over receipts counts that run twice. The reverse case, a failure that is never re-uploaded, means a receipt silently never reaches the worker. For a fleet bench the data still arrives in the task output, but list_receipts will not show it.

Severity is low: no crash and no loss of data on the device, and the receipt is still on the iPad. | fix: Worker (worker/receipts.py ReceiptStore.save): read `receipt.get("receiptId")` and check it against a pattern such as `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$`. While holding the lock, look it up in an index: a dict built at init by scanning the existing files, or a `by-id/<receiptId>` marker file. If the id is already stored, return `{"name": existing, "bytes": len(raw), "duplicate": True}` with 200 and do not write a new file. Otherwise save as now and record id->name. Also add `receipt_id` to summarize(). iPad: on a 2xx, write a sidecar marker (for example `<name>.uploaded`) or keep the set of uploaded names in UserDefaults. On the next bench run, or on scenePhase .active, re-POST receipts that have no marker, with a small retry and backoff. With the worker deduping, these retries and manual taps are safe.
